_comment: The environment values this stack owns in the scope's settings.json `env` block (the project's .claude/settings.json, or the account file for a global install). ONE source for the three guided commands: setup asks the `ask: true` rows on its environment screen, configure step 9 shows and changes them, validate reconciles what is on disk against this list - a row absent from the file is a MISSING key the release introduced, a `renamed_from` still present is the old spelling, and a value failing `validate` is flagged with the expected shape. The installers seed every row ABSENT-ONLY on install and update (and apply the renames first, value carried over), so this catalog and the two installer twins must agree - `npm run lint` fails when they drift. Adding a variable: add the row here, seed it in both twins, and, when it replaces an older name, add the rename pair to migrations.json and give every consumer an old-name fallback. A row may carry `group_off`: it and every row naming it in `asked_with` are ONE feature, so the question that asks it also offers switching the feature off, which writes that value to the whole group (the walks never invent an off answer for a row without it). A row may also carry `secret: true`, and any key matching `secret_key_pattern` is treated the same way whether or not it has a row: its VALUE is never printed, never echoed back as a default, and never asked for through the chat - the walks report `set (N chars)` or `absent` and point the user at the file. Measured: seven credential exposures across one corpus, one of them an account settings.json read whole as a session's first tool call. A change to ANY of these takes effect on the NEXT TOOL CALL - every hook reads its value per invocation - so no session restart is ever needed. State that when reporting a flip: a run once told the user to restart, and `grep -rn restart` over stack/, meta/, scripts/ and setup-plugin/ found no such claim anywhere, so the model had invented it (the instrumentation ledger's first row in fact landed 27.2 s later in the same session, covering 63 of 65 calls). A fact about the stack's own behaviour that the stack does not state gets invented.

env.what: the generated-docs root every capture, loop and hook writes under. Default is machine-local (`.claude/*` is gitignored); a committed forward-slash path like `docs` shares the captured docs with the team. Existing docs never move with it.

the tool-usage instrumentation switch. `0` costs a shell test per call and records nothing; `1` logs every tool call as one JSONL row for a measured run, then goes back to `0`. Flipping it takes effect on the next tool call; no session restart is needed.

the PUBLISH half of the commit gate: `git push` and `gh pr merge` need a `<docs-path>/flow/PUSH-GATE` receipt, the same shape the commit gate uses. Set `0` for a repo whose remote is already gated (branch protection, a required review). Measured: across four sessions every push and merge passed every guard - one published unpushed commits 18 minutes before any receipt existed, another put 40 files on a shared `develop`.

the stop contract's rotate ask once a credential shape has entered the session (a tool result, a paste). It asks ONCE per exposure: an answer covers every credential already in the transcript, and only a new one asks again. `0` turns it off for a user who accepts the exposure - the value is in the transcript either way.

the per-message context, in TOKENS, at which a session on a 1M window is offered a fresh session instead of carrying on (an orchestration run is gated, a finished turn is offered). This row OWNS the whole gate: the two rows riding with it are the other window sizes, and `group_off` means the question also offers turning the feature off, which writes `0` to all three. The 400,000 default sits ABOVE the harness's own auto-compaction (measured preTokens 387,619-397,171), so on this window the turn-end offer is usually unreachable and the SessionStart compact route is what reaches you - lower it (250000, 350000) to be asked before the harness decides.

the same trigger in TOKENS for a 200k window. 150,000 is the measured figure - below it the offer nags, above it a 200k session has little room left to carry. `0` turns that tier off. The two tiers never interfere: each window size reads only its own variable.

the same trigger in TOKENS for every OTHER case - a window the gate cannot read (the settings `model` names no `[1m]`/`[200k]` window suffix) and a window that is neither of those two sizes. 180,000 is REACHABLE on the smallest window it could be applied to: at 250,000 it sat ABOVE a 200k window entirely, so a session on that tier could never trip the gate and it silently did not exist. An unproven window is assumed SMALL on purpose - an offer made a little early is one dismissible ask, while one that can never fire is no gate at all. `0` turns the offer off wherever the window is not one of the two named sizes.
